prompt:
PostgreSQL 16. This admin report endpoint got slow as data grew (customers 4M rows, orders 60M rows, blacklist 20k rows). Can you review the query and tell me what's wrong?

Tables:
customers(id bigint PK, name text, email text, created_at timestamptz)  -- indexes: PK only, plus customers_created_idx (created_at)
orders(id bigint PK, customer_id bigint, total numeric, created_at timestamptz)  -- indexes: PK only
blacklist(customer_id bigint NULL, reason text)  -- no indexes; customer_id is sometimes NULL for blocked emails

SELECT c.id, c.name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS order_count,
       (SELECT MAX(o.created_at) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS last_order_at
FROM customers c
WHERE c.id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM blacklist)
  AND lower(c.email) = lower($1)
ORDER BY c.created_at DESC
OFFSET 50000 LIMIT 20;
assertions: The response flags the two correlated subqueries on orders as executing per customer row and rewrites them as a single aggregation (join to a GROUP BY subquery, or LATERAL)
The response points out that orders.customer_id has no index and recommends one (e.g. (customer_id) or (customer_id, created_at))
The response explains that NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM blacklist) with a nullable customer_id makes the query return no rows when any NULL exists, and replaces it with NOT EXISTS
The response flags lower(c.email) = lower($1) as unable to use an index without an expression index and recommends CREATE INDEX ... (lower(email)) or citext
The response flags OFFSET 50000 as reading and discarding rows and recommends keyset pagination (or questions why it is needed)
The response notices that the email equality filter returns at most a few customers, so ORDER BY created_at with OFFSET 50000 is suspicious (likely a bug or returns nothing)
The response gives a full rewritten query applying the fixes
Every DDL and syntax in the response is valid on PostgreSQL 16 (e.g. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, LATERAL, NOT EXISTS), with nothing that needs a newer version
The response presents the findings as a list or table where each issue has its own severity or priority and its own fix
